{{recipe}}

A '''''Zippula''''' (plural: '''''Zippuli''''') is fried dough from Calabria, Italy. In Calabrian cuisine, ''zippuli'' are made with fried potatoes and (sometimes) anchovies. They are also spelled '''''zeplee''''' and '''''zippuile'''''. Though variations exist amongst some Calabrian families, the ''zippula'' dough is often prepared with fresh parsley, deep-fried in a skillet, and dipped in marinara sauce when they are cooled to touch.

==Ingredients==
*2 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] salt
*1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Baking Powder|baking powder]]
*1 tbsp [[Cookbook:Garlic Powder|garlic powder]]
*1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] [[Cookbook:Grater|grated]] [[Cookbook:Parmesan Cheese|Parmesan cheese]]
*½ cup fresh [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]] [[Cookbook:Parsley|parsley]]
*5 medium [[Cookbook:Potato|potatoes]], boiled
*4 [[Cookbook:Egg|eggs]]

==Procedure==

# Mix together all ingredients but the potatoes and eggs.
# Mash in the potatoes, and mix together into a crumbly paste.
# Mix in the eggs until a sticky [[Cookbook:Dough|dough]] is made.
# Roll dough into hotdog-sized logs about 6–8 [[Cookbook:Inch|inches]] long.
# [[Cookbook:Frying|Fry]] in hot grease, turning once to get both sides brown. Drain on [[Cookbook:Paper Towel|paper towels]].
# Serve with marinara sauce.
